hook: Content note: this is a long, claustrophobic experiment log about a man trapped underground, with decomposing human remains, panic and a death by suffocation recorded on his own camera. The object is a charcoal drawing of a hill and a willow tree, and it is classed Safe. Set aside time to read it in one sitting, because the pacing depends on it.
whyItMatters: SCP-3515 shows how much tension a single test log and a head-mounted camera can carry. The bond that forms between the subject and the lead researcher holds the piece together, and the Safe classification sits uneasily beside what the log records. Tagged illustrated and artistic, it keeps returning to the drawing as its quiet centre.
thingsToNotice:
Falling into deep sleep beside the drawing drops D-6042 into a perfect copy of his childhood home, buried on every side in packed earth, while the real house at the same GPS spot is someone else's and the surface team can never reach him. The tunnel he digs upward fills with human remains, at least twelve bodies by the team's count, many in grey rags, and the roots that break through the ceiling belong to no tree near the real house. Dr. Hallard keeps him going with small talk about burgers and calls him buddy, but also presses him to pick up a rotting head for study, and that mix of kindness and use is the emotional core.

The twist arrives in the last collapse: above the fallen roof the roots hang into open black space, the willow from the picture growing over nothing, and when he claws upward he uncovers a corpse in a grey jumpsuit with a number on its chest and his own face; every body, every boot he joked about, was him. When the corpse falls on him the tunnel closes and Hallard can only apologize while he dies of carbon dioxide build-up over the next forty minutes. The surface team digs to fifty metres and finds nothing, and the camera keeps running for days, picking up the sound of digging slowly getting closer, which casts the digging that everyone near the drawing hears in a very different light.
